messages:
june_oncall: Heads up — eu-west-2 GPU node provisioning is spiking FAIL/Timeouts, queue is growing. I see repeated attach errors and kubelet metadata egress timeouts. https://grafana.redwood/graph/gpu-provisioning :rotating_light:
liam_infra: I'm seeing control-plane connections to provider metadata/KMS endpoints timing out from the provisioner. Errors: 
```
error: attach volume: call to kms redwood-eu-west-2 timed out (connect timeout)
node-provisioner: failed to bootstrap, awaiting network
```
june_oncall: Looks like BGP route flap reported by our transit partner to eu-west-2. Provider console shows partial route suppress for a /24 used by our NAT gateway. Ticket opened: 1234567
maria_sre: Recommend immediate mitigation: 1) Shift new inference traffic off eu-west-2 to eu-central-1 (route-level) 2) Allow the provisioner to fallback to smaller VM types (g4dn->g5.xsmall equiv) so we can satisfy queued jobs 3) Enable cpu-fallback for critical short jobs :point_right: decreases perf but keeps prod up
liam_infra: Starting traffic shift for model-group: gen-latency-critical -> route rule to prefer eu-central-1. Running routing command now:
```
# example, internal tool
infractl route set-preference --from-region eu-west-2 --to-region eu-central-1 --selector "model:gen-latency-critical" --weight 0.8
```
june_oncall: infractl returned accepted, initiating canary: 5% -> 20% -> 50%
deploy-bot: Canary initiated for model-group gen-latency-critical: 5% traffic -> eu-central-1
liam_infra: Also lowering autoscaler threshold for dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-central from 70%->55% to speed scale up. Note this will temporarily increase cost. Doing now.
maria_sre: For in-flight node creation failures, set provisioner retry window to 30m and enable fallback-image (quantized 4bit build) to reduce memory pressure. Command:
```
provisioner update --retry-window 1800 --enable-fallback-image quant-4bit-v2
```
june_oncall: Provider support (cloud-support-bot) responded: BGP flap on transit ISP, they are re-advertising routes, ETA 00:45. Ticket 1234567 updated.
cloud-support-bot: Support note: We see intermittent route withdraws from peer AS65009, re-advert will stabilize after ~30-60m. We recommend traffic diversion while routes converge.
liam_infra: Monitoring: queue length reduced after canary to 20%. Node attach errors down from 18/min to 3/min. Still seeing KMS handshake timeouts ~1%.
maria_sre: Action items: 1) Continue route shift until provider confirms stable 2) Keep autoscaler lowered for 45m 3) Post-incident cost estimate and owner for postmortem: @maria_sre 4) Add a permanent fallback route to eu-central in route policy for gpu-provisioning
june_oncall: Noted, I'm on-call for the next 2hrs and will keep a watch. Cost hit estimate from infractl: approx +$5.2k/day if we keep autoscaler relaxed and diversion at 50%
liam_infra: I'll follow up with a temporary firewall exception to allow direct egress to KMS via alternate transit for provisioner (only for bootstrap CIDRs). Patch: `fwctl allow --src provisioner-cidr --dst kms.eu-west-2 --via alt-transit`
cloud-support-bot: Provider updated: routes re-advertised. We see stability for last 120s; recommending gradual rollback of diversion.
june_oncall: Rolling rollback: 50% -> 20% -> 0% over 15m.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete, traffic back to eu-west-2. Metrics: provisioning failure rate at 0.8% (baseline 0.3%).
maria_sre: Leaving follow-ups: retro owner @maria_sre, create runbook entry for transient BGP peering route suppression, add health-check to trigger automatic short-term diversion, and cost alert threshold for autoscaler relax.
june_oncall: Closing incident thread; will file incident report with timeline and logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
